articles.title: The universe is still speeding up, but nobody knows why
articles.summary: A major new analysis challenges recent claims that the universe's expansion is slowing, finding that the evidence for cosmic acceleration remains strong. The findings preserve the leading role of dark energy, while leaving scientists with the enduring mystery of what this strange cosmic force actually is.
articles.content:
An international team of astrophysicists says the universe is still expanding at an accelerating rate, rejecting recent claims that cosmic expansion may have begun to slow.

The researchers challenged a study published last year claiming the growth of the universe is slowing. They argue that the standard interpretation remains intact: a mysterious force known as dark energy is continuing to drive the universe's accelerating expansion.

The team includes two Nobel Laureates and scientists from institutions around the world. According to the researchers, the controversy sparked by the findings reported last November was caused by a misunderstanding in the analysis rather than evidence that scientists' basic picture of the universe had suddenly broken down.

The new paper was published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society.

New Analysis Challenges a Cosmic Slowdown

The study directly responds to research from a South Korean team that claimed the universe may have entered a period of decelerating expansion. That earlier work suggested dark energy, which acts somewhat like anti-gravity, could be weakening with time.

Lead author Dr. Phil Wiseman, from the University of Southampton, said the latest analysis supports the measurements that astronomers have relied on for years.

"The previous and well-accepted measurements were, in fact, fine and our current understanding of the fate of the universe remains robust," said lead author Dr. Phil Wiseman, from the University of Southampton.

"Thankfully we have averted this crisis, but the mystery about why the rate of expansion of the universe is still accelerating remains.

"By proving our measurements are correct, we can get back to trying to understand what this dark energy actually is, rather than wondering if it exists at all."

Supernovae and the Discovery of Cosmic Acceleration

The international research group included Professor Adam Riess and Professor Brian Schmidt, who shared the 2011 Nobel Prize in Physics with Professor Saul Perlmutter.

Their Nobel-winning work relied on observations of Type Ia supernovae, extremely bright explosions produced by white dwarf stars. By studying these events at different distances, the researchers found that more distant objects appeared to be receding faster. That evidence led to the conclusion that the expansion of the universe is accelerating.

That interpretation has remained widely accepted ever since. However, the South Korean study published last year challenged it by arguing that Type Ia supernovae did not all reach the same peak brightness as the universe aged.

If that were true, astronomers could have been misreading the supernova data and incorrectly concluding that cosmic expansion was speeding up when it was actually slowing.

Researchers Identify Problems With the Earlier Analysis

The University of Southampton-led team says it found a key problem in the way the earlier study estimated the ages of the exploding stars. According to the researchers, the previous analysis treated the age of a galaxy as though it were the same as the age of the individual star that later exploded as a supernova.

The team also said the South Korean study did not properly account for the mass of the galaxies hosting the supernovae. Correcting for host galaxy mass is a standard step in modern cosmology that helps scientists make more accurate measurements.

Professor Riess added: "Extraordinary claims require especially careful testing.

"What we find is that when we calibrate these supernovae, accounting for different host environments and populations, the evidence for cosmic acceleration remains remarkably consistent."

Dark Energy Mystery Remains

Professor Mark Sullivan, also from the University of Southampton, said questioning established ideas and observations remains an essential part of the scientific process.

"This is how progress is made. Although this idea did not turn out to be correct, it has opened up new ways of thinking about how supernovae explode and how we can measure dark energy more accurately," he added.

Fellow co-author Dr. Brodie Popovic said the debate also provided researchers with an opportunity to examine the astrophysics of supernova explosions more closely and reconsider the assumptions built into cosmological measurements.

"We've recently been really focused on astrophysics of the explosions and how they impact cosmology," he said.

"This was a good opportunity to go back and go over all of our assumptions - it turns out, yes, we do understand this stuff and we're accounting for it in our cosmology measurement."

articles.personality_title: New study confirms the universe is still expanding faster, keeping dark energy in focus
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Scientists have long known that the universe is expanding, and about 20 years ago, they discovered this expansion is speeding up. This speeding up is thought to be caused by a mysterious force called dark energy. Recently, some researchers suggested the expansion might be slowing down, which would change how we understand the universe.

**What happened** – An international team of astrophysicists, including Nobel Prize winners, studied this question again. They found that the earlier claim about slowing expansion was based on a mistake. Specifically, the previous study mixed up the ages of galaxies with the ages of the stars that exploded as supernovae, and it didn’t properly consider the mass of the galaxies. By fixing these errors, the new research shows the universe’s expansion is still speeding up.

**Impact** – This is important because it confirms the main idea that dark energy is still pushing the universe to expand faster. It means the current understanding of the universe’s fate is still correct. Also, the debate helped scientists better understand supernova explosions and improve how they measure dark energy, strengthening future research.

**What's next step** – With this confirmation, scientists will continue studying dark energy to learn what it really is and how it works. They will also refine their methods to measure cosmic expansion more accurately, using new data and better models of supernovae and galaxies.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Careful new analysis confirms the universe’s expansion is still speeding up, keeping dark energy as the key mystery driving cosmic growth.
articles.personality_title_fr: Une nouvelle étude confirme que l’univers continue de s’accélérer, mettant l’énergie sombre au centre des recherches
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Les scientifiques savent depuis longtemps que l’univers s’étend, et il y a environ 20 ans, ils ont découvert que cette expansion s’accélère. Cette accélération serait causée par une force mystérieuse appelée énergie sombre. Récemment, certains chercheurs ont suggéré que cette expansion ralentissait, ce qui aurait changé notre compréhension de l’univers.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Une équipe internationale d’astrophysiciens, dont des lauréats du prix Nobel, a réexaminé cette question. Ils ont découvert que la précédente affirmation d’un ralentissement reposait sur une erreur. Plus précisément, l’étude précédente a confondu l’âge des galaxies avec celui des étoiles qui ont explosé en supernovae, et elle n’a pas correctement pris en compte la masse des galaxies. En corrigeant ces erreurs, la nouvelle recherche montre que l’expansion de l’univers continue de s’accélérer.

**Impact** – Cela confirme l’idée principale que l’énergie sombre pousse toujours l’univers à s’étendre plus vite. Cela signifie que notre compréhension actuelle du destin de l’univers reste valide. De plus, ce débat a aidé les scientifiques à mieux comprendre les explosions de supernovae et à améliorer leurs mesures de l’énergie sombre, renforçant ainsi les recherches futures.

**Prochaine étape** – Avec cette confirmation, les scientifiques vont continuer à étudier l’énergie sombre pour comprendre ce qu’elle est réellement et comment elle fonctionne. Ils affineront aussi leurs méthodes pour mesurer l’expansion cosmique avec plus de précision, en utilisant de nouvelles données et de meilleurs modèles des supernovae et des galaxies.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Une nouvelle analyse rigoureuse confirme que l’expansion de l’univers s’accélère toujours, faisant de l’énergie sombre le mystère central de la croissance cosmique.
articles.personality_title_es: Nuevo estudio confirma que el universo sigue acelerando su expansión, manteniendo el enfoque en la energía oscura
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Los científicos saben desde hace mucho que el universo se está expandiendo, y hace unos 20 años descubrieron que esa expansión se está acelerando. Se cree que esta aceleración es causada por una fuerza misteriosa llamada energía oscura. Recientemente, algunos investigadores sugirieron que la expansión podría estar desacelerándose, lo que cambiaría nuestra comprensión del universo.

**Qué pasó** – Un equipo internacional de astrofísicos, incluidos ganadores del Premio Nobel, estudió esta cuestión nuevamente. Encontraron que la afirmación anterior sobre la desaceleración se basaba en un error. En concreto, el estudio anterior confundió las edades de las galaxias con las edades de las estrellas que explotaron como supernovas, y no consideró correctamente la masa de las galaxias. Al corregir estos errores, la nueva investigación muestra que la expansión del universo sigue acelerándose.

**Impacto** – Esto es importante porque confirma la idea principal de que la energía oscura sigue impulsando al universo a expandirse más rápido. Significa que la comprensión actual del destino del universo sigue siendo correcta. Además, el debate ayudó a los científicos a entender mejor las explosiones de supernovas y a mejorar cómo miden la energía oscura, fortaleciendo la investigación futura.

**Próximo paso** – Con esta confirmación, los científicos seguirán estudiando la energía oscura para descubrir qué es realmente y cómo funciona. También mejorarán sus métodos para medir la expansión cósmica con más precisión, usando nuevos datos y mejores modelos de supernovas y galaxias.

**Conclusión en una frase** – Un nuevo análisis cuidadoso confirma que la expansión del universo sigue acelerándose, manteniendo a la energía oscura como el misterio clave que impulsa el crecimiento cósmico.
